title: Isaan Tahdig

items.raw: 2 cups (400 g) basmati or jasmine rice — which rice?
3 tablespoons kosher salt, for the parboiling water
2 stalks lemongrass, tender core finely minced
4 makrut lime leaves, center rib removed, very finely shredded
5 tablespoons neutral oil or ghee, divided
Lime wedges, cilantro, mint, sliced shallot

steps.text: Rinse the rice in several changes of cold water until it runs nearly clear, then soak 30 minutes. Drain.

Bring 3 quarts of water and the salt to a boil. Add the rice and boil 5 to 6 minutes, until the grains are soft on the outside but still firm in the center. Drain in a sieve and rinse briefly with cool water.

In a bowl, mix 2 cups of the parboiled rice with the yogurt, egg yolk, lemongrass, half the lime leaves, chilies, fish sauce, and 1 tablespoon oil. Toss the rest of the rice with the remaining lime leaves.

Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a 10-inch nonstick pot or deep skillet over medium heat. Spread the yogurt rice firmly over the bottom in an even layer. Mound the remaining rice on top in a loose pyramid. Poke 5 or 6 holes down to the bottom with the handle of a spoon.

Drizzle the last tablespoon of oil over the top. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel and cover tightly. Cook 10 minutes over medium until you hear steady sizzling, then turn to low and cook 35 to 45 minutes more.
Peek at an edge with a thin spatula; it should be deep golden. If not, give it another 5 to 10 minutes.
Run a spatula around the edge, set a large plate over the pot, and turn it over in one confident motion. Sprinkle the crust with toasted rice powder and serve with lime, herbs, and shallot.

notes.label: The towel matters
notes.text: it absorbs steam that would otherwise drip back and soften the crust.

notes.label: Toasted rice powder
notes.text: toast raw sticky rice in a dry pan until deep golden, about 10 minutes, then grind it fine. Asian markets sell it ready-made.

notes.label: Nonstick pot
notes.text: this is the one recipe where nonstick is close to essential.

notes.label: Serve with
notes.text: what goes alongside or on top? Larb, grilled meat, or a green papaya salad would all suit it.
gaps: what goes alongside or on top?

openQuestion: This is a best guess — Persian crispy-bottom rice (tahdig) made with Isaan, northeast Thai, flavors. I do not know this dish. Whose is it, and how did it come about? What is actually in it — jasmine or basmati rice, and which flavors? Is it served with something on top, like larb?
